title: Improvement of sperm quality through an indication-specific probiotic – An exploratory pilot study
summary:
The purpose of this clinical study is to investigate whether a specially developed probiotic can positively influence the sperm quality of infertile men and to what extent the microbiome (i.e., the totality of all microorganisms) in semen and hormone levels in the blood change as a result of the probiotic.**

The term *probiotic* refers to health-promoting bacteria which, when consumed in sufficient quantities, have a beneficial effect on health.

The bacterial strains included in the preparation represent the most common bacterial classes found in healthy male semen samples. Since men with reduced sperm quality tend to have lower levels of these specific bacterial classes, supplementation with a probiotic containing these strains may offer a promising approach to improving semen quality.

interventions.name: 30 participants take a multi-species probiotic once daily for 120 days.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with diagnosed pathospermia

The ability to begin taking the study medication promptly after inclusion in the study

Signed informed consent form
Exclusion criteria:
Use of antibiotics within the last 4 weeks

Use of probiotics within the last 4 weeks

Intake of explicitly fertility-enhancing supplements within the last 4 weeks

Regular or repeated use of medications known to impair spermatogenesis (according to the package insert)

Severe impairment of semen quality: Oligo-Astheno-Teratozoospermia (OAT) grade III, pronounced parvisemia with an ejaculate volume < 1 ml

Diagnosed gastrointestinal diseases (e.g., Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis) that could impair absorption of the study medication

Congenital or acquired conditions (e.g., diabetes mellitus) or malformations (e.g., Klinefelter syndrome) that affect spermatogenesis

Immunocompromised individuals

Internally diagnosed conditions requiring medical treatment (e.g., cancer, liver dysfunction, severe heart disease)

Necessity to take antibiotics during the intervention phase
